methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: This paper focuses on developing a data-driven model to predict energy consumption in a twin-screw granulator (TSG) within the DiPP. The model, based on second-degree polynomial regression, demonstrates strong predictive accuracy with R-squared values exceeding 0.8. By optimising energy performance indicators, this work aims to improve the sustainability of pharmaceutical manufacturing processes.

baseline_construction_method.value: Past DiPP campaign data were divided into TSG-activity slices; each torque profile was fitted with y = k × ln(x + 1), poor-fitting slices were removed, and the retained speed, feed-rate, L/S-ratio and k observations were used to select a second-degree polynomial regression model.
evidence_quote: Taking the τ (t) curve from each slice, and performing y = k × ln (x + 1) regression on every torque profile curve;
Dropping all slices where their τ (t) curve does not have a satisfactory fit onto a logarithmic regression model;
Finally, collecting all (ω, F, λ) and (k) pairs for regression analyses.
As can be seen from Table 2, the best regression model produced was a second-degree polynomial regression.

validation_types.evidence_quote: After splitting the dataset appropriately (taking sklearn’s recommended values of a 50/50 split for training and testing data), the data were inputted into various regression solvers provided by sklearn as illustrated in Figure 5. The goal was to test a variety of regression models to see which one would provide the best fit for the data. The full list of regression models used is shown in Figure 4, and the results of the regression analysis including RMSE (root-mean-square deviation) and R2 (R-squared) values are shown in Table 2.

identifies_model_limitations.evidence_quote: The limitation of the y = k × ln (x + 1) model occurs when plugging in large t values. This is because the model predicts unreasonably large torque values with increasing t, which becomes unrealistic for practical applications. Therefore, caution is advised when using this model for extrapolation, particularly at high t values.

proposes_treatment_mechanism.evidence_quote: Such a feature would be extremely useful as it would allow for our model to learn from longer “slices” of TSG activity, as the current model was only trained on shorter “slices” in the range of 50 to 400 s, while real-world processes run for many hours if not days continuously.
